..
Another round of high-end scattered showers for Guam and Rota and
numerous showers for Saipan and Tinian is expected this evening, 
slightly tapering down after midnight. The back-end of Tropical 
Depression 24W (discussed in the Tropical Systems section below) is 
the culprit for widespread cloud cover and towering convection this 
evening. Isolated thunderstorms and locally heavy rainfall are still 
possible tonight as TD 24W continues moving north and away from the 
islands. As for the long-term, scattered showers and isolated 
thunderstorms remain a possibility for all islands through the entire
forecast period as the monsoon trough lifts north, trailing behind 
TD 24W. The zones remained split to convey a slight difference in 
shower coverage over Guam and Rota versus Saipan and Tinian should 
the monsoon trough's northward motion be relatively slow. In 
addition, wind directions appear to be slightly different between the
two zones. There is still high uncertainty regarding flooding 
concerns as ensembles greatly differ in terms of intensity and 
distribution of rainfall. This situation will continue to be 
monitored over the coming week.

Marine...
Combined seas are expected to be 5 to 8 ft throughout the entire
forecast period, with Saipan and Tinian most likely on the higher
end due to their proximity to TD 24W's northeasterly swell. Gentle to
moderate winds out of the north and northwest will turn to the west
for all islands on Thursday. Surf is not expected to reach any 
hazardous criteria at this time, however, a smaller, long-period 
northeasterly swell may cause occasionally elevated waves along north
and east facing reefs. In addition, there is a moderate risk of rip 
currents along all reefs, so remain cautious near and in the waters 
over the next several days. As TD 24W continues moving north, its
corresponding swells may subside a foot or two. Subsequently, the 
monsoonal south to southwesterly swell may increase throughout the 
forecast period.

Tropical Systems...
Tropical Depression 24W continues to struggle (somewhat) to
strengthen further, as it meanders east of Saipan. The 1 PM ChST
position places the LLCC (Low-Level Circulation Center) at 15.5N
148.8E, with its movement being north-northeast at 2 mph. 24W has 
been fighting some dry air entrainment from the northwest to north. 
With that said, vertical wind shear is low (5-10 knots) and warm SSTs
(Sea Surface Temperatures) of 29 to 30 deg. C, and moderate poleward
outflow does make the environment marginally favorable. The latest 
forecast from JTWC (the Joint Typhoon Warning Center) does show 24W 
increasing forward speed dramatically as it lifts off to the north 
over the next 24 hours, becoming a tropical storm as it does so. It 
currently looks to remain east of even the northern CNMI, with the 
Maug Islands perhaps being the closest as the LLCC passes near. 

Eastern Micronesia...
The weather pattern remains fairly quiet across most of Eastern 
Micronesia. The region lies south of the Monsoon Trough which enters
the region near Bikini Atoll, diving southeast to a weak circulation
northeast of Majuro. Meanwhile, a sharp ridge axis extends north 
across the equator and through western Pohnpei State. The surface 
wind flow allows for a ribbon of decent surface convergence to be 
found from near Kosrae to the Majuro and Kwajalein areas. Here, 
scattered weak convection continues to develop, with the main notable
feature being mostly cloudy skies. The lack of greater rainfall is 
tied to the dry air diving south-southwest from the north, due to the
synoptic pattern. 

With that said, the models show a southeast inflow band extending
from TD 24W into the Kosrae and Pohnpei region developing Thursday, 
possibly including Majuro as well. Given some semblance of this 
visible already evident in the streamline analysis and satellite 
data, we kept this expectation in the forecast. However, heading 
towards the weekend, rainfall potential looks to decrease.

As for marine conditions, seas of 4 to 6 feet look to persist into
next week. Light to gentle winds will be common at Pohnpei and
Majuro, but slightly higher in the gentle to moderate range at Kosrae
(as Kosrae will get the "squeeze play" between the ridge axis and 
low pressure circulation). With that said, no hazardous surf is 
expected.

Western Micronesia...
The bulk of the showers have moved north of Palau, and will remain
there through Saturday. Sunday and Monday could see scattered showers
returning as the monsoon band reorients. Winds will be from the west
or southwest at 10 to 15 knots, with occasional gusts to 25 knots
tonight and Thursday. Seas of 5 to 7 feet will diminish slightly to
between 4 and 6 feet by Monday. This will result in marine conditions
that are challenging through Thursday then benign thereafter.
